issue.title: Fix writing-helper strict acceptance parse error

reproduction.environment: Windows final release proof lane in TST-release-validation-2026-04-14
reproduction.result: PowerShell parser error before any HTTP request-level assertions executed
Reproduces the same parser error with mojibake at lines 27, 36, and 43
Script parses and executes; run reached HTTP request path and failed later with 404 because no managed gateway was started

relevant_files.relevance: Primary failure site. The file is UTF-8 without BOM, contains Chinese string literals, and is the only repo script/*.ps1 file with non-ASCII source text. Windows PowerShell misdecodes it and fails before assertions run.
Reusable CI acceptance workflow. Starts the gateway, waits for /health, and invokes check-writing-helper with pwsh. This is the CI equivalent of the local sign-off step.
Operator-facing local sign-off instructions. It tells users to run the acceptance suite in another PowerShell session, which is consistent with the Windows PowerShell reproduction path.
Registers POST /writing-helper/process and POST /writing/helper. Acceptance depends on this route being present after the gateway starts.
Implements writingHelperProcessEndpoint, including local fallback behavior and response shape expected by the acceptance script.
Defines the local helper contract for polish/rewrite/expand/summarize/outline. The strict assertions in the PowerShell script mirror these mode semantics.
Current automated coverage for endpoint parity and local fallback. No test currently covers Windows PowerShell parsing or script encoding behavior.
Release blocker evidence. Records that strict writing-helper acceptance executed 0% of request-level assertions because of the parse failure.
Captures the exact release-proof command order: packaging dry-run, gateway start, strict acceptance, gateway stop, then release summary refresh.
Marks the strict writing-helper command as a blocking L3 release proof step that must pass before refreshed evidence is trustworthy.

dependencies: Windows PowerShell file-decoding behavior for BOM-less UTF-8 source. Current script bytes begin with 70 61 72 61 6D 28 0A 20 and do not contain a UTF-8 BOM.
The acceptance contract of POST /writing-helper/process in src-ts/mcp/endpoints/writing.ts and src-ts/services/writing-helper.ts.
Gateway startup path used by the acceptance workflow and local sign-off instructions: python scripts/start_gateway.py --host <host> --port <port> --log-level <level>.
Release-proof orchestration in TST-release-validation-2026-04-14 and docs/release/SIGN_OFF.md, because the acceptance step is a blocking predecessor to release summary refresh.
existing_patterns: Other scripts/*.ps1 files are ASCII-only; check-writing-helper.ps1 is the outlier that combines PowerShell source with non-ASCII literals.
The repo already keeps writing-helper behavioral parity in TypeScript tests, so the fix should preserve the acceptance contract rather than alter endpoint semantics.
CI uses pwsh for acceptance, while local operator docs say PowerShell generically. The issue is therefore shell/runtime-specific rather than route-logic-specific.

related_changes.summary: chore(scripts): add writing-helper acceptance checker with strict mode
ci(writing-helper): add configurable host for acceptance run

recent_session_context.summary: Earlier release-readiness exploration already identified .github/workflows/writing-helper-acceptance.yml as a formal delivery gate in the authoritative sign-off chain.
Release validation on 2026-04-14 marked the issue as a NO_GO blocker because strict acceptance did not reach request-level assertions.

key_findings: The failure is reproducible on the current 6345c1bc33812fb8f449bef4ec501a9dcda0ae01 revision with Windows PowerShell, so the blocker is real and still present for local Windows sign-off.
The same file parses under pwsh, which isolates the problem to source encoding and shell compatibility rather than endpoint business logic.
Because docs/release/SIGN_OFF.md instructs operators to run the suite in another PowerShell session, the issue affects the documented release procedure even though the CI workflow uses pwsh.
No existing automated test protects against this class of regression. Current tests verify endpoint payload behavior but not Windows PowerShell script load/parse behavior.
A safe fix must keep the acceptance assertions aligned with src-ts/services/writing-helper.ts while making the script parse consistently in Windows PowerShell.
